overview: Scotiabank is one of Canada's Big Six Schedule I chartered banks, providing retail, commercial, wealth management and capital markets services to roughly 25 million customers. It operates through four business segments - Canadian Banking, International Banking, Global Wealth Management, and Global Banking and Markets - with a historical footprint concentrated in Canada and the Pacific Alliance countries of Latin America (Mexico, Peru, Chile, Colombia), though the bank is now actively pivoting capital toward North America (Canada, U.S., Mexico). Fiscal year ends October 31; FY2025 total assets were approximately C$1.46 trillion with net income of C$7.8 billion (C$9.5 billion adjusted).

business_model.summary: Scotiabank earns a spread on loans/deposits (net interest income, ~57% of FY2025 revenue) plus fee-based non-interest income from wealth management, capital markets underwriting/trading, banking fees and insurance. Canadian Banking is the largest and highest-ROE segment; International Banking (Latin America/Caribbean) contributes high-margin but higher-risk retail/commercial banking; Global Wealth Management generates fee-based asset management and brokerage revenue; Global Banking and Markets provides corporate lending, trading and advisory services globally.

revenue_streams.name: Wealth management fees (mutual funds, brokerage, trust)
Trading, underwriting & advisory (Global Banking and Markets)
Insurance and other fee income (incl. KeyCorp associate income)

business_model.customer_type: Mixed: retail/consumer (mortgages, cards, deposits), small business and commercial, corporate/institutional, and high-net-worth wealth management clients
business_model.geographic_mix: Canadian Banking ~44% of net income (FY2025), International Banking (Latin America/Caribbean) ~36%, Global Wealth Management ~22%, Global Banking and Markets ~25% (segment totals exceed 100% due to negative 'Other' corporate segment); reported geographic revenue skews increasingly toward Canada and the U.S. following Latin American divestitures and the KeyCorp stake

main_competitors: Banco Santander, BBVA and local banks in Latin America
KeyCorp and U.S. regional banks (via equity stake and expanding U.S. commercial presence)
competitive_position.market_position: Fourth or fifth largest of Canada's Big Six banks by market capitalization and domestic market share (~13% of Big Six assets), but historically the most internationally diversified of the group via its Pacific Alliance Latin America franchise; recently repositioning toward a North American (Canada-U.S.-Mexico) footprint

moat_factors.description: Canada's concentrated, OSFI-regulated banking sector has very high barriers to entry; the Big Six control roughly 90% of domestic banking assets, limiting new-entrant competition
Long-established retail brand and sticky low-cost deposit base in Canada supports stable, low-cost funding
Four complementary business lines (retail, international, wealth, capital markets) diversify earnings, though 'Other' segment losses and FX volatility complicate reported results
Historically differentiated positioning in Mexico, Peru, Chile and Colombia provided growth exposure unavailable to domestic-only peers, though this is now being partially unwound
14.9% equity stake with board representation gives a toehold into U.S. regional banking and an equity-accounted earnings stream without full acquisition risk

weaknesses: Historically the weakest ROE among the Big Six (FY2025 reported ROE 9.7%, adjusted 11.8%, versus peers often at 14-16%), though closing the gap in 2026
Heavier reliance on volatile, higher-risk emerging-market (Latin America) earnings versus more domestically-focused peers
Below-benchmark 5- and 10-year total shareholder returns relative to the S&P/TSX Composite
Complex multi-year restructuring (Latin America exits, KeyCorp stake, segment reallocation) creates execution and comparability risk for investors
Smaller scale in U.S. capital markets/wealth management versus RBC (City National) and TD (TD Bank, N.A.)

growth_drivers: North American strategic pivot: reallocating capital from Latin America to higher-return Canada, U.S. and Mexico businesses under CEO Scott Thomson's strategy
KeyCorp equity stake (14.9%) providing earnings contribution and a platform for future U.S. expansion (plus tuck-in U.S. acquisitions, e.g., MapleMark Bank in Texas)
Global Wealth Management momentum: record net sales, AUM growth (+16% YoY to approximately C$474B), improving fee mix
Global Banking and Markets record profitability driven by capital markets activity, higher margins and loan/deposit growth
Canadian Banking margin expansion (5 consecutive quarters) and improving credit card/commercial mix
Technology and AI investment (Scotia Intelligence, AI Consortium with Sun Life/TELUS) targeting productivity gains and positive operating leverage
Simplified, less volatile earnings base post-Davivienda/CrediScotia divestitures, improving capital efficiency and ROE trajectory toward and beyond the 14%+ medium-term target

business.risk: Latin America/Pacific Alliance credit and macro risk
business.description: Remaining International Banking exposure (Mexico, Peru, Chile, plus new Davivienda associate stake in Colombia/Costa Rica/Panama) is subject to currency volatility, political risk (e.g., Chile's contested presidential election, Mexico tariff exposure) and higher loan-loss volatility than developed markets

Canadian Banking is heavily weighted to residential mortgages and consumer credit; elevated household indebtedness and mortgage renewal/delinquency trends (management flagged elevated mortgage delinquencies in Q3 2026 despite strong average FICO scores) are a recurring watch item
Concurrent Latin America divestitures, KeyCorp integration, segment reallocation and restructuring/severance charges (C$373M in Q4 2025) create multi-year execution complexity
Intense competition from the other Big Five/Six Canadian banks for mortgages, deposits and wealth management, plus fintech/non-traditional competitors in payments and digital banking

financial.description: NIM (2.33% in FY2025) is sensitive to central bank rate paths in Canada, the U.S. and Latin America; margin benefited from rate cuts and BA-to-loan conversion in FY2025 but could compress if rate cuts stall or reverse
Material earnings exposure to USD, MXN, PEN, COP and CLP; FX translation reduced FY2025 net income by C$85 million and adds volatility to reported (non-constant-dollar) results

KeyCorp investment reduced CET1 by approximately 49 bps; Colombia/Costa Rica/Panama sale reduced CET1 by approximately 13 bps and will generate a further approximately C$300 million after-tax Q1 2026 charge from FX translation release

financial.risk: Provision for credit losses trending higher
financial.description: FY2025 PCL ratio rose to 62 bps from 53 bps, driven by tariff-related macroeconomic outlook deterioration and higher Canadian Banking impaired formations

regulatory.description: As a Canadian Schedule I bank and D-SIB, Scotiabank must maintain CET1, Tier 1, Total Capital, Leverage, TLAC, LCR and NSFR ratios per OSFI guidelines; changes to domestic stability buffer or capital rules directly affect capital deployment/buybacks
Cross-border transactions (KeyCorp stake, Davivienda transfer) require approval from U.S. (Federal Reserve/OCC) and Latin American regulators, creating timing and conditionality risk

Global footprint across multiple AML regimes (Canada, U.S., Latin America, Caribbean, Asia) raises ongoing compliance cost and litigation/legal-provision risk (e.g., Peru VAT-related legal matters, Q4 2025 legal provision of C$74 million)

regulatory.risk: Global Minimum Tax (GMT) and tax regime changes
regulatory.description: FY2025 effective tax rate rose partly due to GMT implementation and shifting income mix across jurisdictions

macro.risk: U.S. tariff policy and trade uncertainty
macro.description: Management explicitly cites U.S. tariffs as weighing on Canadian and Mexican growth outlooks and as a driver of higher performing-loan provisions; stress scenarios model tariffs up to 25% with full retaliation
Bank of Canada and Federal Reserve policy divergence affects NIM, loan growth and credit quality across all segments

macro.risk: Natural catastrophe/climate exposure in Caribbean/Latin America
macro.description: Hurricane Melissa (2026) caused significant damage in Jamaica and the Dominican Republic, both Scotiabank markets, illustrating recurring catastrophe risk to the Caribbean franchise
As a large diversified lender, earnings and provisions are cyclical and sensitive to Canadian and Latin American economic slowdowns

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Canadian banking is a mature, concentrated oligopoly with modest single-digit loan growth; Latin American banking offers higher structural growth but with more volatility; global wealth management and capital markets activity are recovering with record net sales and underwriting activity in 2026
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - earnings tied to interest rate cycles, credit provisioning cycles, and capital markets activity; less cyclical than pure-play capital markets firms due to retail deposit base
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: High - net interest margin and net interest income are directly affected by Bank of Canada, Federal Reserve and Latin American central bank rate decisions
key_input_costs: Provision for credit losses (credit cost of capital)

recent_developments.event: Record Q3 FY2026 results: adjusted EPS C$2.28 (+21% YoY), adjusted ROE 14.2% (exceeding the 14%+ medium-term target ahead of schedule), 10th consecutive quarter of positive operating leverage, CET1 ratio 13.1%
Acquired MapleMark Bank, a Texas-based commercial bank, to support U.S. deposit gathering and organic expansion alongside the KeyCorp stake

Completed sale of banking operations in Colombia, Costa Rica and Panama to Davivienda Group in exchange for an approximately 20% stake (14.99% voting common plus non-voting preferred) in the combined Davivienda Group entity

Recorded C$373 million restructuring/severance charge tied to simplifying Canadian Banking, right-sizing Asia operations within Global Banking and Markets, and regionalizing the international footprint

Recognized a cumulative approximately C$1.4 billion after-tax impairment on the Colombia/Costa Rica/Panama held-for-sale operations; completed sale of CrediScotia Financiera (Peru consumer finance) to Banco Santander

Completed the second-stage (approximately 10%) investment in KeyCorp, bringing total ownership to approximately 14.9% (163 million shares) for approximately US$2.8 billion total consideration; gained two KeyCorp board seats and began equity-method accounting
Board raised CEO Scott Thomson's compensation approximately 28%, reflecting strategic execution progress

Management guided to a further approximately C$300 million after-tax Q1 FY2026 charge related to FX translation loss release upon Davivienda deal closing, alongside an expected approximately 10 bps CET1 benefit from reduced risk-weighted assets

guidance.as_of: Q3 FY2026 Earnings (September 2026) and FY2025 Annual Report (December 2025)

items.notes: Q3 FY2026 adjusted ROE reached 14.2%, surpassing the 14% target earlier than management's original 2027 timeline; CEO stated 14% is not a ceiling
FY2025 adjusted diluted EPS growth was 9.6% (reported was -3.4% due to divestiture-related charges)

items.vs_prior: maintained; achieved 10 consecutive quarters as of Q3 2026
items.notes: FY2025 adjusted operating leverage was +3.0%; Q3 2026 YTD adjusted operating leverage was 3.9%

items.target: Maintain strong capital ratios (no explicit numeric floor beyond OSFI minimums)
items.notes: CET1 was 13.2% at FY2025 year-end and 13.1% at Q3 FY2026; capital deployed to organic growth (approximately 23 bps) and buybacks (approximately 20 bps) in Q3 2026

items.target: Strong earnings growth in FY2026, driven by NII and non-interest revenue growth across all segments, excluding divestiture impact
items.vs_prior: reiterated in FY2025 40-F annual report outlook
items.notes: Management expects lower provision for credit losses in FY2026, partly offset by a higher effective tax rate and modest expense growth
FY2025 adjusted productivity ratio was 54.5%, still above the medium-term target, improving from 56.1% in FY2024
FY2025 adjusted payout ratio was 60.7% (above target range), reported payout ratio 73.7%; quarterly dividend raised to C$1.10/share effective January 2026

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Scott Thomson emphasized that the North American strategy (Canada first, U.S. second, Mexico third) is ahead of schedule, with 82% of earnings now generated in North America and the 14% ROE target already exceeded in Q3 FY2026; he stated 14% ROE is not a ceiling for the bank. Management flagged continued tariff-related macro uncertainty but noted current U.S. tariff measures affect less than 1% of total bank loans, with stress scenarios modeling up to 25% tariffs with full retaliation. Management also highlighted elevated but FICO-strong Canadian mortgage delinquencies as an area of continued monitoring.

bull_case: North American strategic pivot is working ahead of schedule: ROE already exceeded the 14% medium-term target in Q3 FY2026 (14.2%), with management signaling further upside and 10 consecutive quarters of positive operating leverage

De-risked earnings mix after Latin America divestitures (Colombia/Costa Rica/Panama to Davivienda, CrediScotia Peru) reduces exposure to the most volatile emerging-market operations while the bank retains minority equity stakes for optionality
KeyCorp stake (14.9%) and MapleMark acquisition provide a capital-light entry into the attractive U.S. regional banking market without full M&A integration risk, supplementing organic U.S. growth
Record performance in Global Wealth Management and Global Banking and Markets segments shows diversification is paying off, reducing reliance on Canadian retail banking alone

Valuation and dividend support: approximately 5.6% dividend yield (FY2025), strong capital return program (C$8.3 billion to shareholders over trailing 12 months as of Q3 2026), and a 36% total shareholder return in FY2025 that outperformed the TSX
bear_case: Historically the laggard among Big Six Canadian banks on ROE and long-term shareholder returns (5- and 10-year TSR below the TSX Composite), so the current re-rating requires sustained multi-year execution to prove durable

Residual Latin America/Caribbean exposure (Mexico, Peru, Chile tariff and political risk; Jamaica/Dominican Republic hurricane damage) still introduces earnings volatility atypical of domestic-focused peers
Canadian mortgage/household debt concentration leaves Canadian Banking exposed to a housing-driven credit cycle, with management already flagging elevated delinquency trends
Provision for credit losses is rising (62 bps in FY2025 vs. 53 bps in FY2024) on tariff-driven macro deterioration, which could further pressure earnings if the trade environment worsens

Heavy restructuring charges (over C$1.4 billion divestiture impairment, C$373 million severance) and reported-basis ROE/EPS declines in FY2025 illustrate that adjusted metrics mask real near-term GAAP earnings volatility from the transformation
